feedback.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet  $\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1 & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ (z+1)^{2} & =3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1) \\ (z+1) & =\pm \sqrt{3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1 & \ge 0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}=1$, including its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 1}.
$$
